question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party, the Central Military Commission, and key institutions ahead of the 2027 National Congress, with analysts noting continued personnel appointments favoring loyalists and the absence of a designated successor. Recent military purges and elite reshuffles have reinforced his authority, while age norms and party rules no longer constrain extended tenure following prior constitutional changes. Traders assign a 95.5% probability that he remains in power through the end of 2026, reflecting this structural dominance and the low frequency of abrupt leadership transitions in the post-Mao era. Plausible shifts could stem from an unforeseen health event, a severe domestic crisis, or rapid escalation in cross-strait tensions that undermines elite cohesion, though these remain low-probability contingencies based on current evidence.
